newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks 30 pct hike in FY'98 budget for HUD.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks 30 pct hike in FY'98 budget for HUD.

text.p: President Clinton on Thursday proposed $24.8 billion in funding for the Department of Housing and Urban Development in fiscal 1998, up a steep $5.6 billion, or 30 percent, over current levels.
HUD Secretary Andrew Cuomo told a press briefing that the $5.6 billion would help HUD avert its "greatest crisis" in housing programs ever.
He was referring to unprecedented level of rental assistance contracts that are expected to expire in fiscal 1998 under the department's "Section 8" program.

That program, which will face heavy scrutiny by the U.S. Congress this year, subsidizes housing for about 4.4 million low-inome people, HUD says. Contracts for 1.8 million housing units are set to expire in fiscal 1998, the department adds.
Cuomo pledged that HUD would put in place a number of Section 8 reforms in fiscal 1998, including new curbs for the private landlords that get Section 8 subsidies in return for renting to the poor.
For instance, HUD would cut any "excessive" subsidies that landlords are getting and lower the amount of rental increases that landlords could charge, Cuomo said.

Cuomo said Clinton's HUD budget also would provide $100 million to fund a second round of empowerment zones and enterprise communities, which are designed to stimulate job creation in high-poverty areas.

He said HUD also wants $25 million to clean up and redevelop abandoned industrial sites in cities. And it wants to fund the Community Development Block Grants program at $4.6 billion, the same level as fiscal 1997, he said.
HUD also wants to fund construction of more than 110,000 units of affordable housing for some of the neediest Americans through the so-called HOME program next year, Cuomo said.
And HUD wants to provide $50 million to help cities transform abandoned land into neighborhoods of single-family homes called "homeownership zones," he said.
HUD also would fund Ginnie Mae's efforts to stimulate $1 billion in mortgage lending to inner cities, he said.
